Frequently asked questions How much does property management cost on the Sunshine Coast? Fees vary by agency, property and service scope. Ask each property manager for a written schedule covering management, letting, renewal, inspection, tribunal and advertising charges before signing. What does a property manager do in Queensland? A property manager advertises the property, screens tenants, prepares the tenancy agreement, collects rent, arranges routine inspections, coordinates repairs and provides regular statements to the landlord. People performing regulated real estate work in Queensland must hold the appropriate licence or registration. How is the rental bond handled? In Queensland, rental bonds for general tenancies are capped at 4 weeks rent and must be lodged with the Residential Tenancies Authority (RTA) within 10 days of receipt. How often can rent be increased? For general tenancies in Queensland, at least 12 months must generally pass between rent increases. Periodic-tenancy increases require at least two months written notice; fixed-term increases have additional agreement and notice requirements. Exemptions can apply, so confirm the current RTA rules.
